name: A Carousel for Missoula
unique: A hand carved carousel built by 1,000 volunteers over four years, with 38 horses, a dragon chariot and a band organ, in a glass pavilion by the river.
buzz: The story of the volunteers is on the walls and the ride is two dollars; children pick the dragon and adults look at the carving.

name: Smokejumper Visitor Center
unique: The base where the smokejumpers train, with a loft of parachutes, a plane you can walk through and a film on jumping into fires.
buzz: The plane and the gear are the exhibits and the jumpers are often there training; it is free and the tour is short.

name: Rattlesnake Wilderness
unique: A roadless area that starts at the edge of Missoula, with a creek trail into alpine lakes and enough climb to feel remote in an hour.
buzz: Locals run it after work and the lake is a half day; the trail is shared with mountain bikes on some sections.

name: Giant Springs State Park
unique: One of the largest freshwater springs in the country, pouring 156 million gallons a day into the Missouri, with a trout hatchery and a riverwalk.
buzz: The spring pool and the rainbow trout are the stops and it is free; the River's Edge Trail continues for miles along the Missouri.

name: C.M. Russell Museum
customer: Western art people, history fans, families
unique: The largest collection of Charles Russell's paintings and sculpture, plus his log studio and the cabin where he worked, in his hometown.
buzz: The studio and the watercolors are the reason art people come; the museum explains how a cowboy became the west's painter.

name: Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center
unique: A center on the portage the expedition made around the Great Falls, with a full size canoe, interactive exhibits and trails to the river overlooks.
buzz: The portage story is the part of the expedition people do not know and the center tells it well; the trails outside are free.

name: Pictograph Cave State Park
unique: Three rock shelters with painted figures up to 2,000 years old, excavated in the 1930s, on a rim above the Yellowstone valley.
buzz: The pictographs are faint and the story is the archaeology; the loop trail is short and the view of Billings is the bonus.

name: ZooMontana
unique: A small zoo focused on northern climates, with grizzly bears, wolves and a sensory garden, on the Yellowstone River rimrocks.
buzz: The grizzlies and the wolves are the reason to come and the zoo is small enough for two hours; it is good with young children.

name: Moss Mansion
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A 1903 sandstone mansion built by a cattle and banking family, with original furnishings, a ballroom and a staircase that curves three stories.
buzz: The woodwork and the family story are the tour; the October ghost tours are the local tradition.

name: Whitefish Mountain Resort
unique: A locals' mountain above Whitefish with tree skiing, a long groomer from the summit and a view into Glacier National Park from the top.
buzz: Skiers like the lack of crowds and the tree runs; the summit is windy and the base lodge is dated in a good way.

name: Flathead Lake
unique: The largest natural freshwater lake west of the Mississippi, 28 miles long with orchards along the east shore and islands you can camp on.
buzz: The cherries in July and the water in August are the two seasons; the lake is deep and cold and the wind comes up in the afternoon.

name: Lake Como
unique: A mountain lake at the end of a valley in the Bitterroots, with a beach, a campground and trails up to a waterfall and a ridge.
buzz: The lake is the easy family swim and the waterfall trail is the hike; the road is gravel for the last stretch.

name: St. Mary Peak
unique: A 9,351 foot peak in the Bitterroot range with a fire lookout on top and a view into Idaho, reached by a steep trail from the valley.
buzz: Hikers call it the best day hike in the Bitterroots and the lookout volunteer will show you the map; the trail is long and exposed.

name: Daly Mansion
customer: House tour people, gardeners, history fans
unique: A 50 room Georgian revival mansion built by a copper king, with original furnishings, a carriage house and 46 acres of lawns and gardens.
buzz: The house is enormous and the family story is the tour; the grounds are free and the summer concerts are the local event.

name: Kootenai Falls
unique: One of the largest free flowing waterfalls in the northwest, where the Kootenai drops through a gorge, with a swinging bridge over the river to the far side.
buzz: The swinging bridge is the thrill and the falls are the photograph; the trail is steep in places and the river is not for swimming.

name: Ross Creek Cedars
unique: A grove of western red cedars up to 12 feet across and 1,000 years old, with a flat loop trail through the trunks in the Cabinet Mountains.
buzz: The scale of the trees is the surprise and the trail is easy; the road in is gravel and the grove is quiet even in August.

name: Libby Dam
unique: A concrete dam 422 feet high on the Kootenai with a visitor center, a tour inside the powerhouse and a reservoir that runs 90 miles into Canada.
buzz: The tour into the dam is the reason to stop and the lake is beautiful; it is free and the guides explain the flood control.

name: Museum of the Plains Indian
unique: A museum of Plains Indian beadwork, quillwork and clothing from the Blackfeet, Crow and Sioux, with a diorama hall built in the 1940s.
buzz: The beadwork is museum grade and the collection is unexpected for a small town; the annual Indian Days powwow in July fills Browning.

name: Two Medicine Lake
unique: A glacial lake below Rising Wolf Mountain with a 1913 chalet, a boat shuttle and trails to twin waterfalls and a pass into the backcountry.
buzz: The boat across the lake and the hike to Upper Two Medicine is the quiet alternative to the Going-to-the-Sun crowds; the water is cold and the wind is real.

name: Bannack State Park
unique: Montana's first territorial capital, a gold camp of 60 original buildings along a creek, abandoned when the gold ran out and kept as a state park.
buzz: The buildings are unrestored and you can walk into most of them; the July ghost walk and the living history weekends are the local events.

name: Clark Canyon Reservoir
unique: A reservoir on the Beaverhead where Lewis and Clark camped, with trophy rainbow trout and a campground on the shore below the Tendoy Mountains.
buzz: Fishermen come for the big rainbows below the dam and the lake is quiet; the wind makes afternoon boating a chore.

name: Old Montana Prison
customer: History people, true crime fans, families
unique: A territorial prison with cell blocks, a dungeon and a walled yard, plus a complex of car museums and a doll museum on the same ticket.
buzz: The cell blocks and the stories of the 1959 riot are the tour; the car collection next door is the surprise for people who came for the prison.

name: Grant-Kohrs Ranch
customer: History families, ranch people, school groups
unique: A working cattle ranch that was the center of the open range era, with the original bunkhouse, blacksmith shop and a herd of cattle and horses.
buzz: The rangers run the ranch with horses and the bunkhouse tour is the reason to come; it is free and the scale is bigger than a museum.

name: Red Lodge Mountain
unique: A ski hill above a historic coal town with long groomers, tree skiing and a view of the Beartooth range, at half the price of the destination resorts.
buzz: Locals like the price and the lack of lines; the mountain is modest and the town is the reason to stay overnight.

name: Boise Art Museum
unique: A museum in Julia Davis Park with a strong collection of American art and a sculpture garden, next to the zoo and the state historical museum.
buzz: The sculpture garden and the rotating contemporary shows are the draw; it is small enough for an hour and the park is the rest of the afternoon.

name: Idaho State Capitol
unique: A sandstone capitol with a marble dome covered in native copper, and a law library in the basement that looks like a Victorian club.
buzz: The dome and the original chambers are the tour and it is free; the basement library is the room people photograph.

name: Bogus Basin
unique: A nonprofit ski area 16 miles from downtown Boise with night skiing, 2,600 acres and a summer mountain bike park.
buzz: Locals ski after work and the price is the reason; the terrain is gentle and the road up can be snowy.

name: Tubbs Hill
unique: A forested peninsula on Lake Coeur d'Alene with a loop trail, granite cliffs and swimming coves, a short walk from downtown.
buzz: The loop is the local after work walk and the coves are the summer swim; the trail is rocky and the lake is cold.

name: Silverwood Theme Park
unique: A theme park and water park in the Idaho panhandle with a wooden coaster, a steam train and a 1915 carousel, plus a Boulder Beach water park.
buzz: The train and the coaster are the family standards; it is smaller than a California park and the lines are shorter in June.

name: Cataldo Mission
unique: The oldest standing building in Idaho, a church built by Jesuit missionaries and the Coeur d'Alene people with hand hewn timber and painted walls.
buzz: The church and the story of the mission are the tour; the grounds are quiet and the old cataldo town site is a short walk.
